comparator.sourceNotes: The programme-specific 2026-2027 TER defines the 180-EC curriculum for ISAT 56003. The ordinary route represented here assumes the admitted student follows Greek and Latin Language Proficiency rather than a deficiency-transition module: year one is 60 EC, year two is 60 EC, and year three is a 30-EC minor plus 20 EC of Greek and Latin research seminars and a 10-EC thesis. The TER lists Greek and Latin transition modules for students without the relevant VWO final-examination preparation; these are conditional remediation and are not added to the 180-EC standard pathway. The faculty-wide course and minor remain explicit choice space rather than being filled with invented subjects.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes are defensible. The first combines classical literature and myth in translation, rhetoric, ancient philosophy, Greek archaeology, history, material culture and reception. The second follows the independently evidenced question of how antiquity shaped later politics and intellectual traditions; twelve courses / 90 EC differ in each direction. The next generator-backed direction is Greek and Latin language, philology and original-text study, which UCR cannot implement, so production stops at two.

notes.text: Groningen Classics combines cumulative Greek and Latin proficiency and original-language reading with literature, ancient history, archaeology, philosophy, epigraphy, papyrology and field-specific research. UCR can approach antiquity through literature in translation, rhetoric, philosophy, archaeology, heritage, history, law and politics, but it does not teach Ancient Greek or Latin. The UCR programmes therefore offer related perspectives rather than a full Classics curriculum.

The external programme follows a structured Greek-and-Latin sequence, specialist ancient-world seminars, a 30-EC minor and a 10-EC thesis. UCR assembles related material across individually selected courses and has no scheduled thesis; optional independent research is shown only as the standardized comparison element.
